headline: Large User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the cost of grid infrastructure improvements from residential ratepayers to large energy users, primarily data centers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, environmental groups
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Shift Data Center Energy Costs to Large Users
news_summary: Virginia's HB 1393 requires the State Corporation Commission to establish rates that pass the costs of increasing electric generating capacity to customers with 25 MW or more in electric demand, primarily data centers. Governor Spanberger signed legislation directing regulators to assign electricity costs to data centers, aiming to prevent these costs from being passed to other customers.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates data centers to report their water consumption, providing transparency on their environmental impact.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservation advocates
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Mandate Data Center Water Use Reporting
news_summary: The Virginia General Assembly passed SB 553, requiring water suppliers to report the total volume of water provided to data centers to the State Water Control Board. This new law aims to provide transparency on data center water consumption, with reported numbers to be made publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This bill grants local governments more authority over data center siting and establishes noise limits to address community concerns.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, local government associations
opponents: Data center industry, economic development advocates
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Data Center Siting Assessments
news_summary: Virginia's HB 153 mandates that localities require site assessments for new high-energy data centers, examining their sound profile on nearby residential units and schools. While the law forces developers to study noise and disclose substations, it does not explicitly set noise limits or setbacks.
